more.title: North Eastern State Security Minister Engages U.S. AFRICOM on Counterterrorism Efforts - Somali News today Live
more.description: MOGADISHU — The Minister of Security for the North Eastern State administration, Senior Colonel Abdirazak Farah, held a meeting in Mogadishu with senior officials from the United States Africa Command (AFRICOM), focusing on strengthening security cooperation and coordination between the two sides. The meeting, which took place in the Somali capital on September 5, 2026, centered on enhancing regional security and specifically discussed ways to advance collaboration and coordination of efforts to counter security threats in the region. Focus on Capacity Building and Intelligence Both sides discussed elevating their partnership and exchanging expertise, with a view to strengthening the capabilities of the North Eastern State security forces and addressing existing security challenges. The discussions underscore the shared interest in building institutional capacity to manage and mitigate complex security environments. The North Eastern State administration stated that the talks are part of broader efforts to strengthen ties and security cooperation between the regional state and international partners. The meeting also comes amid a broader push by Washington to deepen security ties with Somalia’s regional member states, a strategy that has previously included direct military dialogue with regional administrations. A State in the Making The North Eastern State, formerly known as SSC-Khaatumo, was formally declared as Somalia’s sixth federal member state in July 2025 following a Grand Constitutional Conference in Las Anod attended by 417 delegates representing traditional elders, civil society, political leaders, and community groups from across the region. The state’s formation was officially recognized by the Federal Government of Somalia on July 31, 2025, with Las Anod as its capital. The new state’s leadership has been actively working to establish its institutions and secure its place within Somalia’s federal framework.
